note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated; several rows of the worker measurement table are misaligned by OCR and their values are not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the alates, A. rastratus and A. retifaciens have larger compound eyes and the two ocelli closer together; A. tranquillus is the opposite, with a more inflated postclypeus and the third apical spur of the fore tibia reduced; A. sentosus has a more even cephalic pilosity and a differently shaped fontanelle; A. spinulatus has a longer mandibular apical tooth and a narrower meso- and metanotum. Among the workers, A. rastratus is difficult to distinguish from the present species, with the postclypeus slightly more inflated and the swollen end of enteric valve cushion 1 perhaps slightly broader, though not consistently so; A. sentosus is distinguished by the sclerotized cup and fenestrate base of cushion 1 and by its smaller size; A. spinulatus has a longer mandibular apical tooth, slender spines on cushions 2, 3 and 4, and more spines on the margin of cushion 1; A. tranquillus has a less developed enteric valve apparatus, cushion 1 only partly sclerotized and shorter; A. retifaciens tends to the other extreme, with slender hooked spines on cushions 2, 3 and 4.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity pale yellow, setae sparsely scattered. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27. Mandibular apical tooth rather long, La/Li 0.70–0.71, Ra/Rj 1.00–1.01; a deep notch separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence in surface view, La/L1·Lm 8.90–11.09; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth equal in length, Ra/Ri·Rm 14.99–15.05. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.29–5.64; third apical spur reduced, even absent in some specimens, rarely so in an entire nest series. The midgut–hindgut junction is oblique; the enteric valve seat is joined to the second hindgut pouch by a very short neck, dorsolateral in the unopened abdomen; cushion 1 is sclerotized along its whole length, half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, the margin of the swollen end bearing 15–18 slender spines (mean 16.3), small spines scattered on the stalk and on the concave surface of the swollen end, the base of the stalk with weak transverse wrinkles; the cushions of the other positions bear 3–5 slender curved spines (mean 3.5), abruptly tapering, the tips slightly hooked, with smaller spines over the rest of their length. The valve membrane bears distinct minute spines outside and between the cushions, fringed on small leaflets.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark chestnut brown, not darker above the ocelli; fontanelle much smaller than the ocellus, circular to short-elliptical, its outline ill defined, flat or slightly concave, concolorous with the head capsule; central spot circular or broadly elliptical, flat or slightly raised, as large as or slightly larger than the fontanelle, concolorous; postclypeus chestnut brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark distinct, semicircular, flat or slightly concave, brown; antennae brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum chestnut brown, the dark transverse suture weak on the mesonotum and present on the metanotum; femora and tibiae brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles dark sepia brown, sternites pale brown with a yellowish brown median part, ventral spiracles sepia brown; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule not very evenly rounded, slightly undulate; ocelli relatively rather small, their distance from the compound eye about three quarters to slightly more than their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.23–0.26, posterior margin arcuate, not evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/L1 0.54–0.60, Ra/Rj 0.73–0.89; a distinct notch separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence in surface view, La/Li·Lm 5.90–7.84; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.29–0.33. Cephalic pilosity yellowish brown, the layer rather rough and slightly uneven.
